plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. However, since my value ($35) significantly exceeds the possible maximum value ($20) for any other bidder, I will bid slightly above the maximum possible value to ensure a win. This is because the cost of overpaying (up to $20) is less than the potential profit of winning with a value of $35. I will bid $20.1.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and the payment rule (paying the second-highest bid), the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, the expected value of the highest of the remaining two bidders is approximately (2/3) * 20 = $13.33. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly above this, but considering my value is $41, I can afford to bid higher. I will bid $13.40.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, the expected value is $10. To win, I need to outbid others. However, bidding too high reduces my profit. Since my value is $44, I will bid a small increment above what I estimate the others will bid, aiming for a profitable outcome. I will bid $40.
